why_not_in_the_manifest: The manifest is write-once by design — rewriting it would silently re-label every row already filed under this run. A caveat found after the run is exactly what must not be smuggled into it, so it rides beside the run as its own file.
observed_reasons: rejected by the multiple floor or a distress signal
what_it_records: ROUTING, not the gate. The FAIL reason reads 'rejected by the multiple floor or a distress signal' — one key for two decisions, so a FAIL row does not say which one rejected the name. SEPARATELY, this run also has a POPULATION SKEW — see population_skew.
these_rows_CAN_be_used_for: the admitted/rejected split at the END of the screen (the routing outcome itself)
counting how many candidates reached the G3 stage at all
G1 and G2 gate analysis — those keys are unaffected by this conflation
these_rows_CANNOT_be_used_for: any G3 multiple-floor hit rate or threshold calibration
distinguishing a multiple-floor rejection from a distress rejection
any per-gate FAIL attribution at the G3 stage
comparison against a later run's g3_multiple_floor counts — different populations

superseded_by.note: Runs carrying these recorded the two decisions separately; use those for gate-level questions.

population_skew.what: The screen ran the PREVIOUS universe while this run's grain recorded the CURRENT one.
population_skew.mechanism: `screen_universe` reads `store.latest_universe(reference_date)` — the most recent snapshot AT OR BEFORE the date. Nothing binds that to a `build_universe` run in the same session, and `build_universe` is a separate CLI command. This run read 2026-07-06 while the build wrote 2026-07-29.
population_skew.NOT_the_mechanism: An earlier note said this run took `screen_universe`'s no-snapshot `iter_securities()` fallback. That was an INFERENCE and it is false: the candidate set is set-identical to the 07-06 snapshot, and all 72 overlap names were 07-06 members. Corrected here so the wrong mechanism does not outlive the right count.
population_skew.consequence: 72 tickers carry contradictory rows — screened as candidates while recorded as universe drops. ANY CALIBRATION FROM THIS RUN IS OVER A POPULATION THE SCREEN DID NOT SERVE: the 1800 includes names that were out of band on the run's own reference date.
these_rows_CANNOT_additionally_be_used_f: any rate, base rate or distribution over 'the universe' — the denominator is the prior universe, not this run's
comparison of candidate counts against -02/-03, which screened 1780
gate analysis on the 72 overlap tickers in either direction
population_skew.unaffected: 2026-07-29-02 and -03 both screened exactly 1780, matching their snapshot.
